s.d: pertaining to the very act of doing something
s.g: in the act; in the very activity

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move out of an enclosed or welldefined two or three-dimensional area
s.g: to go out of; to depart out of; to leave from within

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move out of an enclosed or well-defined two or three-dimensional area
s.g: to go out of; to depart out of; to leave from within

s.d: to go out of existence
s.g: to cease to exist; to pass away; to cease

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Birth, Procreation
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to come out from the loins, genitals) to be born as the result of the male role in begetting an offspring
s.g: to be born of; to be begotten by
s.c: In a number of languages it is more satisfactory to speak of the male role in procreation in terms of ‘being the father of’ rather than employing a term which may have undesirable connotations of sexual relations.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Behavior, Conduct
s.d: (idiom, literally: to go in and to go out) to live or to conduct oneself in relationship to some community or group
s.g: to live with; to live among
s.c: The semantic focus of these idioms, especially in ⟦Acts 1:21|Acts 1:21⟧ and ⟦Acts 9:28|Acts 9:28⟧, appears to be the manner in which a person conducts himself in relationship to others, but it is possible to imply a certain amount of movement. For example, in ⟦Acts 1:21|Acts 1:21⟧ it is possible to translate ‘during the whole time the Lord Jesus travelled about with us,’ and in ⟦Acts 9:28|Acts 9:28⟧ one could translate ‘Paul stayed with them and went about in Jerusalem.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus
to listen carefully to and pay attention
s.g: to listen carefully to; to mark someone’s words

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus and an example of obedience and faith
cardinal number, where there are six instances of a countable entity
to announce, with focus upon the extent to which the announcement or proclamation extends{N:001}
s.g: to proclaim throughout; to announce; to speak out about

s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of ἐξαγοράζω ‘to pay a price,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause the release or freedom of someone by a means which proves costly to the individual causing the release
s.c: A literal rendering of ἀγοράζω or ἐξαγοράζω as ‘to release by means of paying a price’ can be misinterpreted in the sense that Christ actually engaged in some kind of monetary transaction. A literal translation may also lead to the mistaken interpretation, which was widespread in the Middle Ages, that in redeeming the believers God actually paid a price to the Devil. Obviously, ἀγοράζω in ⟦1 Corinthians 6:20|1 Corinthians 6:20⟧ and ἐξαγοράζω in ⟦Galatians 3:13|Galatians 3:13⟧ must be understood in a figurative sense.

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to buy out the time) to take full advantage of any opportunity
s.g: to make good use of every opportunity; to take advantage of every chance
s.c: The implication of this statement in ⟦Colossians 4:5|Colossians 4:5⟧ is taking advantage of every opportunity to manifest the reality of one’s faith.

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to redeem the time) to do something with intensity and urgency (used absolutely)
s.g: to work urgently; to redeem the time
s.c: It is also possible to interpret ἐξαγοράζομαι τὸν καιρόν in ⟦Ephesians 5:16|Ephesians 5:16⟧ as ‘to take full advantage of every opportunity’ (see LN 65.42).

s.d: to lead or bring out of a structure or area
s.g: to lead out; to bring forth

s.d: to take something out of its place

s.dp: Danger, Risk, Safe, Save › Cause To Be Safe, Free from Danger
s.d: to rescue or set someone free from danger
s.g: to set free; to rescue; to deliver

s.dp: Think › To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
s.d: to choose out from among
s.c: It is also possible to interpret ἐξαιρέομαι in ⟦Acts 26:17|Acts 26:17⟧ as meaning ‘to rescue from’ (see LN 21.17).

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: to exclude or remove someone from an association
s.g: to exclude; to separate; to get rid of

s.d: to ask for something and to receive what one has asked for
s.g: to ask for with success; to ask and to receive

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event
s.c: In a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness, but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items.

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: to conform as a follower in a detailed or dependent manner
s.c: In some instances it may be necessary to translate ἐξακολουθήσαντες in ⟦2 Peter 1:16|2 Peter 1:16⟧ as ‘to use’ or ‘to repeat,’ since such expressions may fit the context more satisfactorily.

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Imitate Behavior
s.d: to imitate behavior closely (in the NT the imitation involves wrong behavior)
s.c: An equivalent of this expression in ⟦2 Peter 2:2|2 Peter 2:2⟧ may be in some instances ‘many will live immoral lives just as they did.’

s.d: cardinal number, where there are six hundred instances of a countable entity
s.c: The symbolic number in ⟦Revelation 13:18|Revelation 13:18⟧ would result from the total of the numerical values of the letters of the person’s name.

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Application and Removal of Liquids or Masses
s.d: to remove a liquid by wiping off
(a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἐξαλείφω<SDBG:ἐξαλείφω:000000>}[a] ‘to wipe off, to wipe away,’ {D:47.18}) to cause something to cease by obliterating any evidence
s.g: to eliminate; to do away with; to wipe out

s.d: to leap up to a standing position
s.g: to jump up; to leap up
s.c: It is possible that in ⟦Acts 3:8|Acts 3:8⟧ the paralyzed man actually jumped up from the ground, but it is more likely that the reference is to the rapidity with which he got onto his feet.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to come back to life after having once died
s.g: to come back to life; to live again; to be resurrected; resurrection
s.c: In a number of languages there is a difficulty involved in formulating some expression for ‘resurrection’ or ‘living again,’ since such a phrase may refer to what is technically known as metempsychosis, that is to say, the rebirth of the soul in another existence, a belief which is widely held in a number of areas of south Asia. This problem may be avoided in some languages by speaking of ‘his body will live again’ or ‘his body will come back to life’ or ‘he will be the same person when he lives again.’|The phrase ‘the resurrection from among the dead’ may be rendered as ‘to live again’ or ‘to live again after having died.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Grow, Growth
s.d: to begin vegetative growth, with special emphasis upon the sprouting of leaves
s.c: The initial stages of growth, either of a plant as a whole or in the renewal of foliage after a winter or dry season, may be expressed in a number of ways, for example, ‘to become green again,’ ‘to show leaves,’ ‘to see leaves begin,’ or ‘when leaves unfold.’

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Stand
s.d: to stand up in a manner distinct from someone else

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Birth, Procreation
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to raise up seed) the male role in begetting children
s.g: to beget; to procreate; to become the father of
s.c: In contexts such as ⟦Matthew 22:24|Matthew 22:24⟧, ⟦Mark 12:19|Mark 12:19⟧, and ⟦Luke 20:28|Luke 20:28⟧ it may be important to add a note concerning levirate responsibilities, that is to say, the requirement for a younger brother to beget children by a deceased older brother’s wife and the reckoning of such an offspring as being the descendant of the older deceased brother.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Hold a Wrong View, Be Mistaken
s.d: to cause someone to have misleading or erroneous views concerning the truth{N:001}

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event
s.c: In a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness; but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: to be in extreme despair, implying both anxiety and fear
s.g: to be in utter despair; to despair completely

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send out or away from, presumably for some purpose
s.g: to send; to send out; to send forth

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send a message, presumably by someone{N:001}
s.g: to send a message; to send word

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
s.d: to cause a duration to come to an end
s.g: to bring to an end; to end

s.d: to make someone completely adequate or sufficient for something
s.g: to make adequate; to furnish completely; to cause to be fully qualified; adequacy

s.d: to give off or to reflect a very bright light{N:001}
s.g: to glisten; to dazzle; to gleam; to flash

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event
s.c: In a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness; but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to cause someone to live again after having once died
s.g: to raise to life; to make live again

s.d: to cause to come into existence
s.g: to cause to exist; to provide; to raise up
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐξεγείρω in ⟦Romans 9:17|Romans 9:17⟧, see LN 87.38.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: to cause someone to have a higher position and status
s.g: to give higher status to; to raise up; to exalt
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐξεγείρω in ⟦Romans 9:17|Romans 9:17⟧, see LN 13.83.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to move out of an enclosed or welldefined two or three-dimensional area
s.g: to go out of; to depart out of; to leave from within

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of ἐξέλκω ‘to pull, to draw out,’ not occurring in the NT) to cause a change of belief so as to correspond more with the beliefs of the person or factor causing the change
s.g: to draw away; to lead away; to lure away to

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Physiological Products of the Body
s.d: the contents of the stomach ejected through the mouth
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘vomit’ is a descriptive phrase based upon a verb describing the process of vomiting, for example, ‘that which is vomited’ or ‘food that flows out of the mouth from the stomach.’

s.d: to exert considerable effort and care in learning something
s.g: to make a careful search; to seek diligently to learn; to make an examination

s.d: to mark an event as being possible in a highly generic sense
s.c: In ⟦Acts 2:29|Acts 2:29⟧ the possibility of speaking confidently about David evidently is based upon well-known facts.

s.d: to be obligatory; to be within the law
s.g: must; ought to; to be lawful; to be permitted; (with neg.) ought not to

s.d: to engage in a careful search in order to acquire information, though primarily by inquiry
s.g: to try to find out; to make a diligent effort to learn

s.d: to inquire intently, with the implication of careful examination
to provide detailed information in a systematic manner{N:001}
s.g: to inform; to relate; to tell fully
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐξηγέομαι in ⟦John 1:18|John 1:18⟧, see LN 28.41.

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to make something fully known by careful explanation or by clear revelation
s.g: to make fully and clearly known
s.c: For another interpretation of ἐξηγέομαι in ⟦John 1:18|John 1:18⟧, see LN 33.201.

s.d: cardinal number, where there are sixty instances of a countable entity
s.c: Note that ἑξήκοντα in ⟦Matthew 13:8|Matthew 13:8⟧ is not ἑξηκόντακις ‘sixty times.’ The evident meaning here is that some of the seeds grew into plants which produced as many as a hundred seeds; others grew into plants which produced sixty seeds; and still others, only thirty seeds.

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: a day immediately following a previous day{N:001}
s.g: the next day; on the next day

s.d: to cause something to sound forth
a repeated activity
s.g: practice; doing again and again; doing repeatedly
s.c: In a number of languages, however, it may be necessary to restructure this second part of ⟦Hebrews 5:14|Hebrews 5:14⟧ and translate as follows: ‘since they have often judged between good and evil, their abilities to do so are well-trained’ or ‘… they are well qualified to do so’ or ‘… they can easily and correctly do so.’

s.d: cause someone to be so astounded as to be practically overwhelmed
s.g: to astonish greatly; to greatly astound; to astound completely

s.d: to be so astonished as to almost fail to comprehend what one has experienced
s.g: to be greatly astonished; to be astounded

s.d: to think or reason in a completely irrational manner
s.g: to not be in one’s right mind; to be insane; to be mad; to be out of one’s mind; insanity; madness

s.d: to be completely capable of doing or experiencing something
s.g: to be completely able; to be fully able

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: motion from or out of a region (in {S:05801102200012}, the only occurrence of ἔξοδος[a] in the NT, the reference is to Israels departure from Egypt)
s.g: departure; the Exodus; the departure (of Israel from Egypt)

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to depart from life, as a euphemistic expression for death{N:001}
s.g: to leave this life; to die; death; departure

s.d: to destroy and thus eliminate
s.g: to destroy; to destroy and remove
s.c: It is possible in ⟦Acts 3:23|Acts 3:23⟧ that ἐξολεθρεύω refers to a type of severe ostracism.

s.d: to indicate agreement with a proposition or offer
s.c: In some languages one may render ‘he agreed to it’ by simply saying ‘he said, I will do it.’

s.d: to express openly one’s allegiance to a proposition or person
s.c: It is often extremely difficult, if not impossible, to translate ὁμολογέω, ὁμολογία, and ἐξομολογέω by the usual expression for ‘confess,’ since this would usually imply that one has done something wrong. It is normally necessary, therefore, to employ quite a different type of relationship, usually involving a public utterance and an expression of confidence or allegiance. For example, in ⟦Matthew 10:32|Matthew 10:32⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘whoever tells people publicly that he is loyal to me, I will tell my Father that I am loyal to that person.’ Similarly, in ⟦Hebrews 10:23|Hebrews 10:23⟧ one may translate ‘let us hold on to the hope in which we have told people we have such confidence.’ Likewise, in ⟦Romans 15:9|Romans 15:9⟧ one may translate ‘therefore I will tell the Gentiles how I have put my confidence in you.’|For another interpretation of ἐξομολογέομαι in ⟦Romans 15:9|Romans 15:9⟧, see LN 33.359.

s.d: to acknowledge a fact publicly, often in reference to previous bad behavior
s.c: In ⟦Philippians 2:11|Philippians 2:11⟧ the statement πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσηται ὅτι κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός (‘that everyone may confess that Jesus Christ is Lord’) means simply to acknowledge a fact publicly, and in this instance there is no implication of previous bad behavior.|In translating ⟦Matthew 3:6|Matthew 3:6⟧ in some languages, it may be useful to restructure the expression somewhat, for example, ‘they admitted to people that they had sinned’ or ‘they admitted publicly to God …’

s.d: to acknowledge one’s thankfulness, restricted in NT usage to contexts in which God is the one being thanked
s.g: to thank; to give thanks to

s.d: to express praise or honor, with a possible implication of acknowledging the nature of someone or something (occurring in the NT only in quotations from the Septuagint)
s.c: This meaning of ἐξομολογέομαι is almost guaranteed by the parallelism of the second line of the quotation in ⟦Romans 15:9|Romans 15:9⟧, but for another interpretation of ⟦Romans 15:9|Romans 15:9⟧, see LN 33.274.

s.dp: Communication › Swear, Put Under Oath, Vow
s.d: to demand that a person take an oath as to the truth of what is said or as to the certainty that one will carry out the request or command{N:001}
s.g: to put under oath; to insist that one take an oath; to require that one swear
s.c: It is extremely difficult to translate ὁρκίζω, ἐνορκίζω, and ἐξορκίζω in a literal manner, though in some contexts one can say ‘I put you under oath,’ but in a number of passages the person speaking is imploring and not necessarily in a position to command or insist. Therefore, in a passage such as ⟦Mark 5:7|Mark 5:7⟧, one may render the meaning idiomatically as ‘for God’s sake, I ask you, do not punish me.’ In ⟦1 Thessalonians 5:27|1 Thessalonians 5:27⟧ one may translate ‘in the name of the Lord, I ask you to read this letter to all the Christian brothers,’ and in ⟦Matthew 26:63|Matthew 26:63⟧ one may translate ‘in the name of the living God, I charge you, Tell us who you are.’|In most languages one may translate ὁρκίζω, ἐνορκίζω, and ἐξορκίζω by simply adding a causative component to terms meaning ‘to swear’ or ‘to take an oath.’ In other words, ὁρκίζω, ἐνορκίζω, and ἐξορκίζω may be rendered as ‘to cause a person to say under oath.’

s.d: one who drives out evil spirits, usually by invoking supernatural persons or powers or by the use of magic formulas
s.g: exorcist; one driving out evil spirits

s.d: to break something loose, usually by digging out and opening up an area
s.g: to break loose; to take out; to dig out an opening

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Treat Badly
s.d: to ill-treat someone with contempt
s.g: to ill-treat; to ill-treat and look down upon
s.c: Because of the complex nature of the meaning of ἐξουδενέω, it is often possible to translate the term with a semantic doublet, for example, ‘to look down upon and to ill-treat.’ This double meaning can be readily derived from the literal rendering ‘to regard as nothing.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Despise, Scorn, Contempt
s.d: to despise someone or something on the basis that it is worthless or of no value
the right to control or govern over
s.g: authority to rule; right to control

s.d: the domain or sphere over which one has authority to control or rule
a means or instrument by which authority is marked or symbolized
s.g: symbol of authority; symbol of subjection to authority
s.c: This passage, however, is subject to a number of different interpretations, as commentaries clearly indicate.

s.d: one who has the authority to rule or govern
a state of control over someone or something
the power to do something, with or without an added implication of authority
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἐξουσία in ⟦Mark 3:15|Mark 3:15⟧ as meaning ‘authority,’ and in a number of instances it is difficult to determine whether the focus is upon the power which an individual has or a granted authority to do something which naturally implies strength or power (see LN 37.35 - LN 37.38).

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Powers
s.d: (title for supernatural forces and powers) a supernatural power having some particular role in controlling the destiny and activities of human beings
s.g: power; authority; lordship; ruler; wicked force
s.c: Some scholars have believed that it is possible to reconstruct at least in part some of the hierarchy represented by these various supernatural forces and powers, on the basis of the neoplatonic system of nine such powers arranged in three orders of three each. NT terminology and usage does not, however, lend itself to such a classification, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to determine what are the significant differences between these supernatural powers and forces.|In the case of ⟦Ephesians 1:21|Ephesians 1:21⟧ some scholars apply the terms in question both to the supernatural and to the human sphere, thus emphasizing the totality of Christ’s rule. This has a considerable measure of justification in view of the concepts held by persons in the ancient world, since various earthly powers were supposed to reflect corresponding supernatural powers.|For the most part, translators have endeavored to render the various terms in somewhat different ways, for example, ἐξουσία as ‘authority’; δύναμις as ‘power’; κυριότης as ‘ruler’; and phrases such as τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις as ‘wicked spiritual forces in the heavenly world.’ In a number of languages, however, there are simply not enough terms to designate various kinds of powers, authorities, and forces which could be employed in speaking of such supernatural impersonal powers. Accordingly, some translators have simply used a phrase such as ‘any and all kinds of supernatural powers.’ Where it is possible to make certain lexical distinctions between terms and phrases, this, of course, should be done, but in a number of contexts this may be impossible, and accordingly, some explanation in a marginal note may be required if the reader is to understand satisfactorily the intent of the passages in question.

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: the right to judge on the basis of having the potential to evaluate
s.g: right; freedom of choice; freedom of action; power to evaluate

s.d: to rule or reign by exercising authority over{N:001}

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a position of high status

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sleep, Waking
s.d: to cause someone to awaken
s.g: to cause to wake up; to awaken someone; to wake up someone

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sleep, Waking
s.d: pertaining to having awakened
s.g: having awakened; awake after having slept
s.c: In some languages the process of waking up is described idiomatically as ‘when his mind came back to him’ or ‘when his eyes opened.’

s.d: a position not contained within a particular area
s.c: It is also possible to understand ἔξω in ⟦Acts 16:13|Acts 16:13⟧ as involving extension (see LN 84.27).

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension To a Goal
s.d: extension to a goal which is outside a presumed area

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › General
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἔξω<SDBG:ἔξω:000000>}[a] ‘outside,’ {D:83.20}) a person who is not a member of a particular in-group
s.c: See also LN 11.11.

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Body
s.d: (an idiom, literally: the outside person) the physical nature or aspect of a person
s.c: The phrase ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος is to be understood in direct contrast with ὁ ἔσω (ἄνθρωπος) in the same verse, which refers to the psychological or spiritual nature of human personality (see LN 26.1).

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension From a Source
s.d: extension from a source which is outside
a position not contained within a particular area
the outside surface of an object
s.c: The manner in which ἔξωθεν, ἐκτός, and ὄπισθεν may be rendered in particular contexts depends very largely upon what is being spoken about. For example, ἔξωθεν in ⟦1 Peter 3:3|1 Peter 3:3⟧ refers to the outward aids employed in making oneself beautiful, but instead of speaking of such objects as being on the surface or on the outside, it may be necessary to speak of those things which one puts on the body or what one wears.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › General
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἔξωθεν[a] ‘from outside,’ {D:83.20}) a person who is not a member of a particular in-group
s.c: In a number of languages it may be appropriate to render ⟦1 Timothy 3:7|1 Timothy 3:7⟧ as ‘he should be a man who is respected by those who are not believers’ or ‘… by those who are not followers of Christ.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to force someone or something to leave
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to indicate more explicitly the factors involved in driving out the nations, for example, ‘the nations whom God forced to leave their land as our ancestors came in.’

s.d: the movement of a ship being driven ashore
s.g: to run aground; to run a ship onto a beach

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Regions Below the Surface of the Earth
s.d: (an idiom, literally: the outer darkness) a place or region which is both dark and removed (presumably from the abode of the righteous) and serving as the abode of evil spirits and devils
s.c: In a number of languages this expression in ⟦Matthew 8:12|Matthew 8:12⟧ must be rendered as ‘they will be thrown outside where it is dark.’

s.d: to celebrate a festival or feast
s.g: to celebrate; to observe a feast; to participate in a festival

s.d: the events associated with the celebration of a festival or feast
s.c: Though various celebrations of the Jewish religious year have traditionally been called ‘feasts,’ it would be wrong to use a term which would suggest gluttony or wasteful abundance of food. The emphasis should be upon the ceremonial character of the eating rather than upon the extent of what was eaten. Therefore, it may be better in a number of languages to use terms referring to ‘celebrations’ or ‘festivals,’ since the festivities of such gatherings were far more important than the feasting.

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπαγγέλλομαι<SDBG:ἐπαγγέλλομαι:000000>}[a] ‘to promise,’ {D:33.286}) the content of what is promised{N:001}
the content of one’s agreement or approval
s.c: In ἐπαγγελία the focus is upon the communication of agreement or approval. One may, therefore, translate 'and are waiting for your approval´ in ⟦Acts 23:21|Acts 23:21⟧ as 'and are waiting for a message from you concerning your agreement´ or 'and are waiting for word from you as to your approval.´

s.d: to announce with certainty as to what one will do
to announce something openly and emphatically
(derivative of {L:ἐπαγγέλλομαι<SDBG:ἐπαγγέλλομαι:000000>}[a] ‘to promise,’ {D:33.286}) the content of what is promised{N:001}
to cause a state to be{N:001}
s.g: to cause to be; to make to be; to make; to result in; to bring upon; to bring about

s.d: to exert intense effort on behalf of something

s.dp: Linear Movement › Gather, Cause To Come Together
s.d: to gather together in addition to or besides
s.g: to gather together more; to collect (as of crowds)
s.c: In ⟦Luke 11:29|Luke 11:29⟧ it may be more satisfactory to translate ἐπαθροίζομαι as ‘having gotten larger’ or ‘becoming more and more.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the first Christian in Asia Minor
to speak of the excellence of a person, object, or event
s.c: In a number of languages praise can only be expressed by direct discourse, and this requires some content which provides the basis for praise. For example, in ⟦Luke 2:13|Luke 2:13⟧ instead of a literal rendering of ‘praising God,’ it may be necessary to have ‘they said, God is wonderful,’ and in ⟦Luke 16:8|Luke 16:8⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘the master of this dishonest manager said, You are remarkable for having done such a clever thing.’

s.d: to speak of the excellence of a person, object, or event
s.c: In a number of languages praise can only be expressed by direct discourse, and this requires some content which provides the basis for praise. For example, in ⟦Luke 2:13|Luke 2:13⟧ instead of a literal rendering of ‘praising God,’ it may be necessary to have ‘they said, God is wonderful,’ and in ⟦Luke 16:8|Luke 16:8⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘the master of this dishonest manager said, You are remarkable for having done such a clever thing.’

s.d: that which is worthy of or deserves praise
s.g: something worthy of praise; something praiseworthy
s.c: In some languages the closest equivalent of ‘praiseworthy’ is ‘something which people should praise.’

s.d: to cause to move up
s.c: In a number of languages one cannot speak of ‘raising hands,’ since this would imply something that was detached from the body. It may therefore be necessary to say ‘extending hands upwards.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to raise up the head) to demonstrate courage in the face of danger or adversity
s.g: to have courage; to lift the head
s.c: A literal rendering of ἐπαίρω τὴν κεφαλήν ‘to lift up the head’ can be misleading in some languages, since the expression may be an idiom meaning ‘to be proud’ or ‘to try to take precedence over others.’ A more satisfactory equivalent in some languages may be ‘to look up.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to lift one’s heel against) to oppose someone by turning against such a person, possibly with focus upon the initial aspect of becoming opposed to
s.c: In a number of languages a convenient way of rendering ‘to turn against’ may be ‘to become an enemy of.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to lift up the eyes) to direct one’s attention to something by looking closely at
(an idiom, literally: to raise the voice) to increase the volume with which one speaks, so as to overcome existing noise or the speech of someone else
s.g: to raise the voice; to cry out; to speak loudly

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπαίρομαι ‘to rise up,’ not occurring in the NT) to rise up in opposition against

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Trust, Rely
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἐπαναπαύομαι ‘to remain upon something or someone,’ not occurring in the NT) to continue to believe firmly in someone or something and thus to rely upon
s.g: to rely on; to depend on; to put one’s trust in
s.c: The concept of dependence or reliance upon something may be expressed in a number of different ways. For example, the phrase ἐπαναπαύω νόμῳ in ⟦Romans 2:17|Romans 2:17⟧ may be rendered in some languages as ‘you believe that all you need is the Law’ or ‘you believe the Law will help you in every way.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Governmental Administrative Areas
s.d: a part of the Roman Empire (usually acquired by conquest) and constituting an administrative unit ruled over by an ἔπαρχος selected by the Roman Senate
property in which a person was expected to reside, either as the result of ownership or legal contract
s.c: In the NT ἔπαυλις occurs only in ⟦Acts 1:20|Acts 1:20⟧ as a quotation of ⟦Psalms 69:25|Psalms 69:25⟧. The immediate reference is to a person’s traditional residence, but the entire passage must be interpreted figuratively as a reference to a person’s expected position or place of service. The phrase γενηθήτω ἡ ἔπαυλις αὐτοῦ ἔρημος may be rendered as ‘may his house become empty’ or ‘may his home be deserted.’

s.d: to cause foam to occur on the surface of a liquid
s.c: ἐπαφρίζω occurs in the NT only in ⟦Jude 1:13|Jude 1:13⟧ in a figurative context. It probably differs from ἀφρίζω (LN 14.28) in emphasizing the greater degree or extent of foam on the surface.|In some languages the type of foam which would be referred to in ⟦Jude 1:13|Jude 1:13⟧ is called ‘the saliva of the waves’ or ‘the whiteness of the waves.’ Since foaming at the mouth is also regarded as a sign of anger, it is possible to speak in some languages of the foam of the waves as being ‘the anger of the waves.’ In other languages one may speak simply of ‘the whiteness of the waves.’

s.d: to take special notice of something, with the implication of concerning oneself

s.c: Though the terms ἐπιβλέπω, ἐπεῖδον (ἐφοράω), and ὁράω suggest as a result of their central meanings some measure of visual perception, what is involved in these specific contexts is much more than visual perception. The focus is actually upon intellectual activity and concern.
